messages.author: f546d6dbfc5aa09e
messages.subject: Mediation Analysis error: Error in `:=`(IDE, a * b) : could not find function ":="
parts:
I am new to lavaan and r and have been trying to determine indirect effects for a path model I have run. I have tried several different ways of running this and am stuck with errors. After scouring the internet for answers, I am stuck. This is the output I get:

library(lavaan)
+ > 
+     > model <-'
>     + # outcome model
+     + FinalGrade ~ c*Autonomous_T2+b*Class_Difficulty
++FinalGrade ~ c * Autonomous_T2 + b * Class_Difficulty
>     + 
+     + # mediator models
+     + Class_Difficulty ~ a*Autonomous_T2
+++Class_Difficulty ~ a * Autonomous_T2
>     + 
+     + # indirect effects
+     + IDE := a*b
Error in `:=`(+++IDE, a * b) : could not find function ":="
>     + 
+     + # total effect
+     + total := c+a*b
Error in `:=`(+++total, c + a * b) : could not find function ":="
>     + '
+     + 
+     + fitsem <- sem(model,data=RAI_Data_Ready_for_Path,bootstrap = 10000)
+     + summary(fitsem, fit.measures=TRUE, standardize=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)

What am I doing wrong??
J

messages.subject: Re: Mediation Analysis error: Error in `:=`(IDE, a * b) : could not find function ":="
parts: What am I doing wrong??

Judging from all the "+" symbols after the ">" symbols, it looks like you are copy/pasting Console output back into the Console.  Instead, you should be writing your R script into its own ("source") text file, then send commands from that file to the Console.  If you can post your R script itself, it might be easier to see what is going wrong.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Mediation Analysis error: Error in `:=`(IDE, a * b) : could not find function ":="
parts:
Jody,
I ran the following script and obtained no errors.  The summary output included the defined parameters.

model <-'
# outcome model
FinalGrade ~ c*Autonomous_T2+b*Class_Difficulty
 
# mediator models
Class_Difficulty ~ a*Autonomous_T2
 
# indirect effects
IDE := a * b
 
# total effect
total := c + a * b
'

require(lavaan)
fit <- lavaan(model, data=NULL, do.fit=FALSE)
summary(fit)

So, I believe that your problem is not your script but rather they manner in which you are attempting to execute it.  Most R GUIs have a tool button, menu option, or keyboard shortcut for running sections of R script.  If you must paste the script manually into the console, make sure that you have a '>' prompt with no '+' signs.  Those should only appear in the console within your model syntax.  The errors that you received were not lavaan errors but R interpreter errors.  The R interpreter cannot parse lavaan model syntax.  The jumble of prompt symbols prevented R from accepting your model syntax as one continuous string. 

If that does not help, try describing the process that you are using to execute your script.

Keith

messages.subject: Re: Mediation Analysis error: Error in `:=`(IDE, a * b) : could not find function ":="
parts:
Jody,
I have never used rStudio and do not have it installed.  However, I asked one of my doctoral students who uses rStudio.  She said the following.

There are two convenient ways to execute a script in rStudio.  Make sure that you have an open console with a '>' prompt and the script open in a separate script window.  Option 1 is to use the "run" tool button in the upper right of the script window.  Option 2 is to select the lines you want to run and type <Ctrl><Enter>.  Be sure that the script window is the active window before trying to run the script.

If you have a '+' prompt, you probably have an incomplete R command pending in your console.  You can try clearing that with the <Esc> key.  (In the GUI that I use, <Ctrl>c works.)  If nothing works, the nuclear option is just to shut down R and start again with a fresh console.

As noted earlier, "+" prompts are normal as part of executing multiple line scripts when a command carries over across lines, such as lavaan model syntax strings.  The critical thing is to start with a '>' prompt before you execute the script.  Under no circumstances should you encounter a double '+' prompt.  You should begin and end with a '>' prompt, '+' prompts in between are not a problem.

If the above does not solve your problem, you probably need to provide a detailed description of the steps that lead up to the problem.  You may need to provide screen shots.

Keith
